decision:
The unanimous overturn from OPEN to NARROWED is CONFIRMED. The verifiers did not share an error on the grade. Verifier 2 overstated one finding, discrepancy (ii), and the corrections below fix it.

Why OPEN falls. The audit graded OPEN for one reason only: the source was unread. This pass READ it in GMMPS v1's text layer, scratchpad/d64/L4/galanda.txt. Its md5 4bac4a9400afceac615c5aa3b9f83c6e matches the pin.

Prop. 4.10 (offset 145266, p.48), verbatim: 'Consider a1, a2 ∈ R and b0, b1, b2 ∈ R \ {0}'. It also requires that (4.19) 'admits three and only three independent solutions ... in D'. Its conclusion is about the local form (real β_i, P zero-free on [4m^2, ∞), (4.16)), not about growth. The tree's (T2) therefore matches the source, but the three-solution condition is dropped.

Thm 4.16 (offset 172122, p.58), verbatim: 'Consider Z, the set of zeros of Q(w^2) given in (4.30). If Z ⊂ (−4m^2,0) and if S ∈ C∞c(M), the solution (4.31) of (4.9) are bounded in time. Furthermore, they decay at least as t^−3/2 ... If Z ⊂ (−4m^2,∞), with some γ ∈ Z, γ > 0, the solution is exponentially growing.'

Z is defined below (4.31) as the zero set of Q in C\(−∞,−4m^2), in Q's own w^2 variable. I re-derived F_S(−w^2) + Q(w^2) = 0 identically with sympy; the tree pins the same identity at linstab.py:954. So a growing F_S zero γ < 0 is a Q zero x = −γ > 0. That falls under the GROWTH clause. The interval (−4m^2, 0) is the hypothesis of the BOUNDED/DECAY clause.

The tree at linstab.py:142-144 attaches that decay interval to the growth conclusion.
- Read in x, no growing zero satisfies it (z3 unsat, with vacuity controls sat).
- Read in γ, it imposes a cap |γ| < 4m^2 that the source does not impose.
- In both readings it drops the growth clause's requirement that the whole of Z be real and lie in (−4m^2, ∞), with some element > 0. GMMPS's own sec. 5.1 has complex-conjugate zeros for smaller b_2, and there the growth clause does not apply.
That is a dropped hypothesis plus a misattributed interval, which is NARROWED by the rubric.

Why not another grade.
- Not WRONG: no source statement is contradicted.
- Not STANDS: the tree's hypotheses are not the source's.
- Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum enters Q (4.30), which carries only m, a_i, b_j and J.

The tree's load-bearing inference survives at source.
- At α~^S_1 = 0 the root γ = 0 sits at x = 0. That is in neither clause: it is not in the open interval (−4m^2, 0) (z3 unsat), and it is not > 0 (z3 unsat).
- With b_0 = 0 it is also outside Prop. 4.10.
- So ALPHA_ZERO_ROOT_GROWTH = 'OPEN' (linstab.py:352) and 'outside Thm 4.16 and Prop. 4.10' are correct. The reason at :179 is incomplete but not false.
- GMMPS's reported S root, x = 3.32e-62 m^2 > 0, is in the growth range, provided all of Z is real.

Re-runs, all in adjudicate/run/:
- the audit's rederive script: ALL PASS;
- verifier 2's verify script, including the vacuity negations and the real-J Planckian root: ALL PASS;
- verifier 1's thm416_variable_map.py: PASS;
- my adj_check.py, a sympy identity plus z3 clause membership with vacuity controls: ALL PASS.

Divergences between the verifiers, settled by reading:
(1) TT with b_0 = 0. Sec. 5.2 says 'since b0 = 0, there is no need to find h0', and p.62 then says 'according to Proposition 4.10, if we find three independent zeros...'. The source applies Prop. 4.10 where its hypothesis b_0 ≠ 0 fails. That is a source-internal discrepancy, as verifier 1 has it. Verifier 2's 'consistent' overstates.
(2) Audit discrepancy (i) dissolves. R6 tested the tree's interval, not the source's.
(3) R7 is mis-framed: in (4.31) a simple zero at x = 0 gives (1/Q′(0)) G^0_ret, a massless propagator, not t/C.

The proof's decay paragraph prints (−4m^2, ∞). Read literally that would include x = 0, but it is a misprint, and the statement governs. Whether (4.31) settles γ = 0 is new work under a named hypothesis (simple zero, (4.31) valid). It is not a finding of the source.
corrections_to_record: Audit: the OPEN grade rested only on 'source not read'. The source is READ (galanda.txt, md5 4bac4a9400afceac615c5aa3b9f83c6e; Thm 4.16 at offset 172122, p.58; Prop. 4.10 at offset 145266, p.48), and the grade is NARROWED.

Tree, linstab.py:142-144: the interval (-4m^2, 0) is Thm 4.16's BOUNDED/t^-3/2 DECAY hypothesis. Growth requires Z ⊂ (-4m^2, ∞) with all of Z real (no complex-conjugate zeros) and some element > 0. There is no upper bound, and growth goes as ~e^{sqrt(L) t} for the largest zero L.
Z is the zero set of Q in its own w^2 variable. F_S(γ) = -Q(-γ), so a growing F_S zero γ < 0 is a Q zero x = -γ > 0. The audit's guess that Z is taken in γ is answered the other way by the text.

Prop. 4.10: b_0, b_1, b_2 ∈ R\{0} matches verbatim. The tree omits the hypothesis that (4.19) has three and only three independent solutions in D. The proposition's conclusion is the local form, not growth.
Audit discrepancy (i) DISSOLVES: the 'Planckian for O(1)' b_2 roots are in the growth range at source, subject to all of Z being real. R6 tested the tree's interval, not the source's.
Audit R6 puts the Planckian root at -|b1/b2| ≈ -1.1e60 m^2, neglecting J. With real J it is ≈ -1.6e61 m^2 (verifier 2). The verdict is unchanged.

Audit discrepancy (ii) is a SOURCE-INTERNAL DISCREPANCY, settled by reading. Sec. 5.2 skips h_0 because b_0 = 0, yet p.62 invokes Prop. 4.10 for TT, where b_0 ≠ 0 fails. TT a = 4m^2 is also the endpoint Prop. 4.12 excludes. Verifier 2's 'consistent' overstates this.
Audit R7 is mis-framed: w^2 = s^2 + p^2, and a simple zero at x = 0 contributes (1/Q'(0)) G^0_ret(S), a massless retarded propagator, not t/C. It is heuristic and not load-bearing.
Audit script: R4's docstring claims a zero exists on γ < 0, but the code checks only F_S(0) > 0. 'a_TT = 4m^2' is tautological in the script.
Tree, linstab.py:179: the reason γ = 0 lies outside Thm 4.16 names only the decay interval. The growth clause's strict γ > 0 also excludes it. The conclusion holds.

Source misprints (discrepancies, not refutations): (a) the proof writes Z ⊂ (-4m^2, ∞) for the decay estimate; read literally this would cover x = 0, but the statement governs. (b) The proof writes Q'(-γ) and S^(±√γ, 0), inconsistent with Z defined in w^2. (c) Sec. 5.1 writes '(5.3) equals Q(-w) for ξ = -w^2'; correct is F_S(-w^2) = -Q(w^2). (d) p.62 has 'cat' for 'cut'.

Line numbers in the tree have shifted: the restatement now begins at linstab.py:142 (interval at 144), not 143. ALPHA_ZERO_ROOT_GROWTH is at 352. The other sites (177-179, 344-349, 954, 1054-1055) are current. linstab.py is unchanged since its 2026-09-25 commit, with no working-tree diff.

tree_sites.finding: Thm 4.16 is restated as growth 'for Z strictly inside (-4m^2, 0)'. The restatement takes the decay clause's interval and drops the growth clause's all-Z-real condition, Z ⊂ (-4m^2, ∞). The audit cited this as 143-145.
The provenance 'text layer via alphaXiv, body read in full' is consistent with the held text layer.

The OPEN, 'outside Thm 4.16 and Prop. 4.10', holds at source: x = 0 is in neither clause, and b_0 = 0 fails Prop. 4.10. The reason given omits the growth clause's strict γ > 0 and Prop. 4.10's three-solution hypothesis.

The 'other growing roots', including the Planckian ones for O(1) b_2, are in Thm 4.16's growth range at source only if all of Z is real. Sec. 5.1 has complex zeros for smaller b_2. The audit's 'outside the theorem' is withdrawn.
LITERATURE_SPLIT_IS_ONE_CONSTANT uses the same 'other growing roots' wording, and the reality-of-Z hypothesis is unnamed.
The WITHDRAWN replacement text 'outside GMMPS Thm 4.16, Prop. 4.10 ...: OPEN' is consistent.
The check F_S(-w^2) = -Q(w^2) was re-derived independently. It is the identity that fixes Z's variable.
The record pin of ALPHA_ZERO_ROOT_GROWTH is consistent.
The sec. 5.2 TT quote is accurate. The source itself skips h_0 because b_0 = 0, yet invokes Prop. 4.10 at p.62. That discrepancy is in the source.
